claims.text: Engineered nano-columnar grain boundaries act as distributed nucleation sites for the magnetostructural phase transformation.
Local strain modulation at the engineered grain boundaries reduces the transition energy barrier.
Reducing the transition barrier by grain-boundary engineering broadens the phase transition.
Grain-boundary engineering reduces hysteresis during magnetic-cooling cycles below 1 T.
The engineered films retain a significant magnetocaloric effect despite transition broadening.
Conventionally sputtered, ambient-condition FeMnNiGeSi films have a relatively coarse and weakly structured grain morphology.
Varying substrate temperature and applying a 900 °C, 30 s rapid thermal anneal can induce nano-columnar grains with increased grain-boundary density.
A greater density of nano-columnar boundaries enables a more gradual and spatially distributed phase change.
A more gradual and distributed phase change reduces the abruptness of the transformation.
Fine grain structure promotes faster heat exchange.
Engineered thin films will exhibit a broader magnetostructural transition than the cited ingot and microribbon baseline.
Engineered thin films will exhibit less hysteresis than the cited ingot and microribbon baseline.
Transition broadening will moderate the peak magnetocaloric entropy change.
The engineered thin films will have improved cooling efficiency.
Systematic changes in substrate temperature will produce progressive shifts in transition temperature.
Systematic changes in substrate temperature will correlate with progressive hysteresis reduction.
Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons of FeMnNiGeSi have a uniformly ordered hexagonal structure.
The ingot and microribbon baseline undergoes a first-order magnetostructural transformation.
The ingot and microribbon baseline has a large, abrupt, and hysteretic magnetocaloric response.

contradictions.description: The initial state is defined as an as-deposited sputtered thin film, but the predicted comparison calls arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons the 'as-deposited bulk baseline.' This makes the operative control ambiguous and confounds microstructure engineering with sample geometry and processing route.
The target is repeatedly described as an as-deposited film, while the proposed engineered state receives a subsequent 900 °C rapid thermal anneal and therefore is not as-deposited.
